org_cost_calculator.title: Cost Calculator
org_cost_calculator.subtitle: The Price of Silence for the Organization

intro.title:
Bullying is an
expensive choice.
intro.text:
Zero tolerance is often just a word. When we turn the malaise associated with bullying into numbers, it becomes a strategic risk that management is forced to address.

Let's calculate what an 'unquestionable culture' costs your organization annually.

result.title: Bullying costs {{amount}}€ per year.
result.subtitle: Estimate is based on {{count}} affected employees.
result.box1_text: This calculation implies no reputational damage or potential legal costs, which can easily double the sum. Presenteeism (employee is present but efficiency has dropped) is often an invisible 'leak' consuming thousands of euros a month.
result.box2_text: An intervention that reduces bullying by only 20% pays for itself with {{savings}}€ savings in the first year alone. Cultural change is not just humanity, it is a productivity leap.

culture_thermometer.title: Culture Thermometer
culture_thermometer.subtitle: Organization Health Check

intro.title:
What kind of air
do you breathe?
intro.text:
Culture doesn't change with posters, but with daily actions and a sense of safety. This thermometer measures psychological safety and structural protection anonymously.

Answer honestly based on current status.

questions: I can raise concerns about workplace behavior without fear of negative consequences for myself.
My supervisor reacts consistently when someone behaves inappropriately.
In our team, difficult issues can be discussed openly without a norm of silence.
I feel I am treated fairly in task distribution and feedback.
I clearly know how to report bullying suspicions and I trust the process.
I have seen a situation (within 12 months) where inappropriate behavior was addressed quickly.
There are no 'untouchable' people in our team due to their position.
If I made a mistake, I wouldn't expect to be humiliated or isolated.
In my workplace, there is a clear difference between firm feedback and bullying.
Management's actions show that bullying has real consequences.

result.title: State of Culture
result.safety_desc: This figure tells how freely employees dare to be themselves and raise issues without fear of humiliation or retaliation.
result.risk_desc: This figure describes the credibility of management, processes, and intervention. The higher the number, the harder it is for bullying to take root in structures.
result.critical: Measurement shows critical deficiencies in either sense of safety or structures. This state exposes the organization to prolonged bullying cases and expensive turnover.
result.strong: Your organization has a strong foundation. Continue open dialogue and ensure no 'untouchable' favorites are created through the LMX phenomenon.

intro.title: Leadership Blind Spots
intro.text:
The manager is the gatekeeper: your choices in decisive moments either cut off bullying or make it part of everyday life.

Test your ability to identify and intervene in three decisive moments.

scenarios.title: Decisive Moment 1: First Signal
scenarios.description: In a team meeting, you notice a 'joke' that clearly confuses and silences one member. Others laugh.
scenarios.choiceA: Stop it: Address it clearly immediately or right after: 'I noticed this, I want to ensure it doesn't happen again.'
scenarios.choiceB: Ignore: 'It's just their humor,' you think. If I intervene, I ruin the good mood.
scenarios.feedbackA: Correct. By stopping even small things, you signal that laughing at someone's expense is not part of the culture.
scenarios.feedbackB: Risky. Inaction normalizes the behavior and signals that this kind of game is part of the deal.

scenarios.title: Decisive Moment 2: Official Report
scenarios.description: An employee comes to you and says: 'I feel like I'm being treated inappropriately.'
scenarios.choiceA: Take seriously: Thank them for their trust, document, explain the process, and agree on a timeline for investigation.
scenarios.choiceB: Downplay: 'You might be a bit sensitive, you know Lisa just has that style.'
scenarios.feedbackA: Great. The psychological contract is maintained when the organization responds as promised and appropriately.
scenarios.feedbackB: Dangerous. The reporter feels left alone and the threshold to tell in the future grows. The psychological contract breaks.

scenarios.title: Decisive Moment 3: Follow-up
scenarios.description: The matter has been clarified and boundaries agreed upon. Weeks have passed and the situation seems to have calmed down on the surface.
scenarios.choiceA: Active monitoring: Ensure agreed actions, keep regular check-ins with both parties.
scenarios.choiceB: Assumption: You assume the matter is over because no one comes to complain anymore.
scenarios.feedbackA: Essential. Bullies often just change target or tactic. Continuous monitoring guarantees change.
scenarios.feedbackB: Error. Silence does not mean a solution. Often it just means giving up or fear of reporting again.

items.title: React (Signal)
items.desc: Do not belittle even the smallest inappropriateness. It is a seed that takes root if watered by silence.

items.title: Register (Report)
items.desc: Document everything. Objective data is a manager's best friend when things start to be unraveled.

items.title: Resolve & Monitor
items.desc: Ensure actions bite. Monitor at 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months. Bullying is removed only with persistence.

analysis_steps.title: What is the risk?
analysis_steps.desc: Direct intervention can increase risk if you are unsure of safety.

analysis_steps.title: What is the goal?
analysis_steps.desc: The most important thing is to break the isolation and show support.

empathy.title: Mirror Neuron Rescue
empathy.subtitle: Experience the situation through another's eyes

steps.speaker: Matt
steps.text: You are in the break room. You hear three colleagues laughing at Janne's new idea across the room. Janne sits alone at a table staring at his coffee cup.

choices.text: Go sit next to Janne and start chatting about something else.
choices.feedback: Good! You broke the isolation.

choices.text: Shout at the group: 'Stop that trash talk!'
choices.feedback: Brave, but you escalated the situation.

choices.text: Continue drinking coffee so you don't become a target yourself.
choices.feedback: You protected yourself, but Janne was left alone.

steps.speaker: Janne
steps.text: Thanks for coming. It felt a bit... weird to be alone.

choices.text: Of course. Their behavior was inappropriate.

steps.speaker: Group
steps.text: The group falls silent and stares at you angrily. Janne looks uncomfortable.

choices.text: Go to Janne anyway.

steps.speaker: You
steps.text: You leave. You feel a sting in your heart as you see Janne left alone.

choices.text: Try again later.

intro.title: Are you a silent witness?
intro.text:
Most workplace bullying happens in front of others. The bystander's reaction – or lack thereof – determines if bullying continues.

In this module, you will learn 5 safe ways to intervene.

questions.scenario: In a team meeting, the manager sighs heavily and rolls their eyes whenever Matt speaks. Others start snickering.
questions.explanation: Repeated, non-verbal humiliation and creating peer pressure is bullying, not 'humor'.

questions.scenario: A colleague disagrees with the project direction and argues their point strongly but professionally in a meeting.
questions.explanation: Disagreeing and debating are part of work, as long as it doesn't get personal.

questions.scenario: A colleague consistently 'forgets' to invite Lisa to lunch and team coffees, even though everyone else is invited.
questions.explanation: Social exclusion (ostracism) is one of the most common and damaging forms of bullying.

responsibility.title: Bystander Effect & Responsibility
responsibility.text: See what happens to the probability of intervening when there are more witnesses.
responsibility.explanation_alone: When you are the only witness, you feel 100% responsibility and are likely to act.
responsibility.explanation_group: The more people there are, the more we assume 'someone else' will handle it. This is called diffusion of responsibility.

cheat_sheet.title: Delegate
cheat_sheet.desc: Ask for help from others or a manager.

cheat_sheet.title: Delay
cheat_sheet.desc: Support the victim after the situation.

scenario.speaker: Situation
scenario.text: You are in the break room. You hear two colleagues talking loudly: "Did you hear what the new guy messed up again? Unbelievable incompetence." The new employee sits at the next table and hears everything.

choices.text: Go sit next to the new employee and ask: "Hey, how is your project going?"
choices.feedback: Great! You distracted attention from the bullies (Distract) and offered support without confrontation. This is often the safest way.

choices.text: Say loudly: "Hey, we don't talk about colleagues like that."
choices.feedback: Brave! Direct intervention makes the boundary clear. However, always assess your safety before confrontation.

choices.text: Go to the new employee later: "I'm sorry about their behavior, it wasn't cool."
choices.feedback: Important! Delayed support (Delay) is vital. It removes the victim's doubt that they might have imagined the situation.

scenario.speaker: Narrator
scenario.text: The new employee smiles with relief and starts chatting with you. The bullies go quiet for a moment and then change the subject as the 'audience' disappeared.

choices.text: Continue

scenario.speaker: Narrator
scenario.text: The room goes silent. One of the speakers mumbles "it was just a joke", but the conversation stops. The new employee gives you a grateful look.

choices.text: Continue

scenario.speaker: Narrator
scenario.text: The new employee sighs: "Thanks for saying that. I thought I imagined it all." You validated their experience, which is critical for recovery.

choices.text: Continue

boundaries.title: Before You Intervene...
boundaries.text: Heroics don't help if you burn out yourself. Remember the safety checklist:
checklist: Do I have power/status in this situation?
Can I make the situation worse by intervening now?

intro.title:
It's not character.
It's biology.
intro.text:
When you switch your brain to 'war mode' for a long time, it starts to change. The same mechanisms that once saved you now prevent focus and joy.

Good news? The brain is plastic (neuroplasticity). We can 'rewire' it for safety.

amygdala.title: Amygdala
amygdala.desc_text: Constantly scans for threats. After trauma, it's hyperactive – screaming 'DANGER!' even if you sit safely at home.

prefrontal.title: Prefrontal Cortex
prefrontal.desc_text: Responsible for logic, regulating emotions, and making decisions. Under stress, this part 'shuts down' so energy goes to pure survival.

hijack.title: Amygdala Hijack
hijack.text: When stress levels rise too high, your wisest part loses control.
hijack.btn_breathe: Breathe: Return control to the ruler
hijack.btn_stress: Stress: Let the amygdala take over
hijack.quote: You are not stupid or insecure – your brain is just saving energy for survival.

repair.title: Rewiring
repair.text: Your brain changes based on what you practice. Every day.

item1.title: Name the feeling
item1.text: When you say 'I am scared', you activate the prefrontal cortex and the amygdala's scream fades.

item2.title: Somatic work
item2.text: Calming the body (like shaking) sends a message to the brain: 'The danger is over'.

item3.title: Small wins
item3.text: Your brain needs evidence of safety. Do one small, manageable thing at a time.

summary.title: Recovery has begun.
summary.text: Your brain has done its best to protect you. Now it's time to teach it that it can rest. Be patient – growing connections takes time, but it happens with every repetition.

intro.title: Why does the body remember?
intro.text: Trauma and chronic stress are not just 'in your head'. They are stored in the body as tension, vigilance, or numbness. For the mind to calm down, the body must first feel safe.

shake.title: The Shake
shake.desc: Release adrenaline by shaking the body.

steps.text: Stand up if you can.
Start by shaking your hands.
Include your shoulders.
Shake your whole body.
steps.instruction: Like a dog getting out of water.

steps.text: Stop and feel the flow.

breath.title: Box Breathing
breath.desc: Lower heart rate with rhythmic breathing.

steps.text: Breathe in...
Hold...
Breathe out...
Hold...

ground.title: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding
ground.desc: Bring your mind to the present using senses.

steps.text: Find 5 things you see.
Find 4 things you can touch.
steps.instruction: Feel the texture with your fingers.

steps.text: Find 3 sounds you hear.
Find 2 things you smell.
Find 1 thing you can taste.
steps.instruction: Or feel the taste in your mouth.

steps.text: Clench your fists...
And let go completely.
Pull your shoulders to your ears...
Drop your shoulders down.
Squeeze your eyes shut tight...
Let your face melt into relaxation.

debrief.title: How does your body feel now?
debrief.text: Even a small moment of nervous system calming helps recovery. You can return to this whenever you feel hyper-alert or numb.

intro.title:
Safety
Restoration
intro.text: Trauma and prolonged stress tune the nervous system to a constant state of alarm. In this exercise, we learn to calm the body and identify safe havens.

grounding.title: Grounding
grounding.text: When anxiety strikes, bring attention to the present moment with the 5-4-3-2-1 technique. Try this now.

things you can touch

anchors.title: Safety Anchors
anchors.text: List places and people with whom you are completely safe.

summary.title: Exercise Completed!
summary.text:
You have created a safety plan for yourself.
Remember: Safety is not just a place, it is a state in your nervous system.
summary.hint: Return to these in your mind whenever you feel threatened.

action_protocols.title: Response Toolkit
action_protocols.subtitle: Concrete Action Models
action_protocols.description: Don't freeze. Here are ready-made words and plans, so you know exactly what to do.

acute_scripts.intro_text:
Three steps to manage chaos.
1. Stop: Pause your reaction (breathe).
2. Speak: Set the boundary.
3. Document: Write it down immediately.

public_mockery.title: Public Mockery
public_mockery.script: I do not like this comment. Stop it immediately.
public_mockery.nuance: Calm, low voice. No smiling. Eye contact.

withholding_info.title: Withholding Info
withholding_info.script: I need this information for my work. Send it now.
withholding_info.nuance: Don't ask 'could you'. State the need. CC a representative if repeated.
withholding_info.next: Screenshot your request. if no answer, send reminder.

isolation.title: Isolation
isolation.script: Why wasn't I invited? Add me in the future.
isolation.nuance: Ask directly in a meeting or chat. Make the invisible visible.
isolation.next: Ask the team: 'Did you notice I was missing?'

difficult_conversation.title: Difficult Conversation Formula
difficult_conversation.intro: Use this 5-step framework in a private discussion.

steps.title: 1. Opening
steps.script: Thank you for coming. I want to discuss our interaction. This is important for my work.
steps.tip: Frame neutrally. Don't blame, invite to discuss.

steps.title: 2. Concrete Example
steps.script: In last Tuesday's meeting you said publicly 'You don't get this'. I experience this as dismissive. How does that sound to you?
steps.tip: State fact (what happened) and impact (how it felt). End with open question.

steps.title: 3. Boundary
steps.script: In the future, I expect the snide remarks to stop. My work flows best without it. Do you agree?
steps.tip: State clear requirement. Don't ask for permission, but commitment.

steps.title: 4. Follow-up & Support
steps.script: How do we ensure this doesn't repeat? Do I need anything from you?
steps.tip: Share responsibility for the solution. 'How do we succeed in this?'

steps.title: 5. Closing & Documentation
steps.script: Thanks for the talk. I'll note this down. Anything to add?
steps.tip: Make it official. Send a memo by email (CC representative).

manager_chain.title: Manager is the Bully?
manager_chain.intro: When power is misused, you must protect yourself with bureaucracy. Don't wait. Document everything.

steps.script: I find [action] inappropriate. I ask you to stop.
I am reporting [Undisputable facts]. I need a clarification.
I need help resolving this. Attached: documentation.
Bullying causes symptoms. I request a statement on work capacity.
Employer has not taken action despite notification.

safety_plan.title: My Safety Plan
safety_plan.intro: Fill this out and save a screenshot on your phone.

form.reaction_placeholder: E.g. I leave the room for 5 mins.
form.phrase_value: I am using my safety plan now – I need help.
form.exit_placeholder: E.g. If no change in 3 weeks -> Sick leave.
form.place_placeholder: E.g. Cafe at lunch / Remote work.
form.disclaimer: Data is not saved on server for privacy. Take a screenshot.

exit_strategy.title: Exit Strategy
exit_strategy.subtitle: When is it time to leave?

intro.title:
When is it time to
Leave?
intro.text: Leaving is not giving up. It is sometimes the only correct strategic move to protect your health. This tool helps you assess the situation objectively.

signs.title: Early Warning Signs
signs.subtitle: Select all that you recognize in your situation.

list.repetition: Repetition: Situations repeat weekly and are not random.
list.exclusion: Exclusion: I am repeatedly left out of information or invites.
list.health: Health: I experience physical symptoms (stomach pain, insomnia) when thinking about work.
list.normalization: Normalization: Inappropriate behavior is dismissed as 'humor' or 'house style'.
list.target: Targeting: Criticism is directed at me personally, not my work.

manager_test.title: Manager Test
manager_test.subtitle: How has the manager or management reacted to the situation?

questions.text: Manager intervened within a week of notification.
Manager listened to both parties equally.
A clear written plan with follow-up was made.
Manager belittled the situation or advised to 'ignore it'.
Retaliation or pressure occurred after notification.

manager_test.insight: Did you know? Studies show intervention fails in 60-80% of cases if management is passive. Management support is critical.

traffic_light.title: Your Assessment
traffic_light.subtitle: Based on the signs you observed and management action.

red.desc: Signs indicate the situation is dangerous to health and no change is in sight.

yellow.desc: The situation is worrying. Active monitoring and Plan B are needed.

green.desc: There are still opportunities for corrective moves, but be vigilant.

stat_box.title: Statistical Fact:
stat_box.text: People typically leave within 6-12 months when health starts to fail. Don't wait for burnout.

plan.title: Action Plan
plan.subtitle: Take control. Here is a proposal for next steps.

section1.title: Secure Your Back
items: Visit occupational health to document symptoms.

section2.title: Mental Detachment
items: Focus on leisure and identity outside work.
Define a 'backdoor' (e.g. study leave or savings).

target_date.title: Target Date
target_date.text: Set a deadline for yourself. If the situation hasn't improved by then, fully activate Plan B.

intro.title:
Return home.
To your own body.
intro.text: When the mind races or feels numb, grounding returns you to this moment. It is not about removing thoughts, but shifting attention to where you are safe: the now.

exercises_view.title: Small moments of presence
exercises_view.quote: "Grounding is a skill that strengthens with every repetition."

observation.title: Conscious Observation
observation.description: Choose one object and study it as if seeing it for the first time.
observation.content_intro: Pick up or look at an object in front of you. Notice:
steps: How does light reflect off its surface?
If you named three different color shades in it, what are they?
observation.hint: This exercise interrupts automatic thought chains by anchoring the mind to the present.

sound.title: Soundscape
sound.description: Close your eyes and find the farthest sound you can hear.
sound.content_intro: Stop and listen. Do not name sounds, just listen to them as waves:
steps: What is a sound coming from outside your current space?
Do you hear your own breath or the rustle of clothes?
What happens in the silence between sounds?

anchor.title: Safety Anchor
anchor.description: Find a physical touch point that reminds you of safety.
anchor.content_intro: Press palms together or place hand on heart. Feel:
steps: The warmth of your hand against your skin.
Say in your mind: "I am here, in this moment it is safe."

summary.title: Be kind to yourself.
summary.text: These exercises are always with you. You can do them on the bus, in a meeting, or just before bed. Every time you anchor yourself, you teach your nervous system that there is space to rest in this moment.

intro.title:
Brain stuck?
It's the rumination network.
intro.text:
When we do nothing, the "Default Mode Network" (DMN) activates in our brains. After trauma, it turns into rumination: an endless chain of past wrongs and future fears.

It is not thinking. It is the brain's way of trying to solve the impossible.

explanation.title: DMN: "The Worrier of Yesterday"

rest_illusion.title: Illusion of Rest
rest_illusion.text: DMN activates when the "focused network" shuts down. After trauma, the brain doesn't know how to rest, instead it starts replaying traumatic memories trying to find a solution.

loop.title: The Loop
loop.text: Rumination is like running in circles in a forest: you are active but getting nowhere. This consumes huge amounts of energy and prevents recovery.

explanation.action: See what the loop looks like

simulation.title: Cycle of Rumination
simulation.subtitle: Your brain repeats these phrases thousands of times a day.
phrases: What if I had done differently?
simulation.hint: "Recognize that this is your brain's automatic loop."

breakout.title: How to stop the DMN?
breakout.subtitle: Rumination only stops by changing the state.

tools.title: Focused Sense
tools.text: The brain cannot ruminate and focus on senses at the same time. Feel your soles on the ground or touch a surface.

tools.title: Name the Loop
tools.text: Say to yourself: 'Now my brain is ruminating again.' This specificies control to the prefrontal cortex.

tools.title: Concrete Action
tools.text: Do something physical. Clean a shelf, walk across the room, open a window. Change the environment.

summary.title: The cycle is broken.
summary.text: Your brain tried to protect you by worrying, but now you know it leads nowhere. Choose conscious focus instead of rumination whenever you notice the loop starting.

difficult_conversations.title: Difficult Conversations
difficult_conversations.subtitle: Choose an opponent and practice setting boundaries safely.

ui.won_desc: You maintained your professionalism and boundaries.
ui.lost_desc: Emotions took over or you gave up your boundaries.

aggro.title: The Aggressor
aggro.intro: LISTEN TO ME! Why is this report late?! Are you completely incompetent??

dialogs.opponent: This is total bulls**t! I can't believe we pay you a salary!

options.text: Sorry, I try my best...
options.reply: Trying isn't enough! Do your job!

options.text: Do not speak to me like that.
options.reply: I speak how I want when there are no results!

options.text: We will discuss when you calm down. Inappropriate behavior does not help.

victim.title: The Victim
victim.intro: Why do you always persecute me? I've had it so hard...

dialogs.opponent: Don't I ever do anything right in your opinion? *sob*

options.text: No, you don't do wrong, you see...
options.reply: You always explain! You hate me!

options.text: We are discussing the task, not you as a person.
Stop that crying.

gaslight.title: The Gaslighter
gaslight.intro: What are you talking about? I never promised that. Are you imagining things again?

dialogs.opponent: You have a vivid imagination. Are you stressed?

options.text: Maybe I am... do I remember wrong?
I have an email with the date.
options.reply: Emails can be faked or misinterpreted.

options.text: The fact is this. I discuss documents, not memories.
options.reply: You are so uptight... but fine.

intro.title: Why do good people do nothing?
intro.text:
Have you ever seen bullying and frozen? It's not because you are a coward.

It is the Bystander Effect, a psychological phenomenon that prevents helping in group situations. Once you understand the mechanism, you can break it.

diffusion.title: Diffusion of Responsibility
diffusion.subtitle: "Someone else will handle it."
diffusion.explanation: When you are alone, you know help depends on you. In a large group, we subconsciously assume someone else is more qualified or ready to act.

evaluation.title: Evaluation Apprehension
evaluation.subtitle: "What if I mess up?"

pressure.title: Audience Pressure
pressure.text: We fear overreacting. What if it was just a joke? What if others think I'm difficult?

risk.title: Social Risks
risk.text: At work, we fear loss of status or being labeled a 'snitch'. This is a natural, evolutionary defense mechanism.

evaluation.solution: 💡 Solution: Lower the threshold. Intervening doesn't have to be heroic. A small distraction or question is enough.

ignorance.title: Pluralistic Ignorance
ignorance.subtitle: "No one else is reacting, so there is no emergency."

reveal_shown.title: Everyone is uncertain.
reveal_shown.text: Everyone looks at others' "calm" expressions and thinks they are the only one worried. In reality, everyone is just trying to hide their fear.

steps.title: Recognize the phenomenon
steps.text: When you notice hesitation, remember: "This is just the bystander effect."

steps.title: Act first
steps.text: Even one voiced concern breaks pluralistic ignorance. Others will follow.

intro.title: It's not your memory.
intro.text:
Gaslighting is manipulation aimed at making the target doubt their own perception, memory, or sanity.

It is a subtle process that erodes self-esteem piece by piece. But when you learn to recognize the code, it loses its power.

tactics.title: What they say vs. What happens
tactics.subtitle: Click cards to see behind the scenes.

items.phrase: You are way too sensitive, it was just a joke.
items.translation: They try to minimize your experience and shift focus away from their action.
items.description: Makes your feelings 'wrong', causing you to doubt your own reactions.

items.phrase: That never happened. You remember wrong.
items.translation: They lie directly to change the course of history.
items.description: The most dangerous form. When repeated enough, you start trusting their memory instead of yours.

items.phrase: Why do you always start a fight? You clearly have issues.
items.translation: They make you the problem to avoid responsibility.
items.description: Changes the subject by attacking your character ('ad hominem').

stages.title: Descent into Fog
stages.subtitle: Gaslighting doesn't happen at once, it is a slow process.

items.name: Disbelief
items.text: You think they must be mistaken or confused. You don't take it personally yet.

items.name: Defense
items.text: You try to argue and prove you are right. You use huge energy defending yourself.

items.name: Depression
items.text: You start believing you are the broken one. You doubt every thought and feeling.

reclaim.title: Reclaim Reality
reclaim.subtitle: Manipulation breaks when examined in light.

items.title: Write things down immediately
items.text: Phrases, times, and your own feelings. Documentation is an anchor that keeps you in reality.

items.title: Trust 'reality checkers'
items.text: Talk to friends or colleagues who know you. They help you see you are not going crazy.

items.title: Stop arguing
items.text: The Gaslighter will not apologize. The most important thing is that YOU know the truth. You don't need to prove it to them.

summary.title: Truth is strong.
summary.text: Now that you know these tactics, you are a harder target. Do not let anyone write your history for you. Your perception is valuable and true.

idealist.title: The Idealist
idealist.desc: You place justice above all. You are brave, but may get into conflicts that jeopardize your own position.
idealist.advice: Your courage is admirable. However, remember to choose your battles so you don't burn out.

pragmatist.title: The Pragmatist
pragmatist.desc: You look for solutions that work in practice. You try to balance results and people.
pragmatist.advice: Your diplomacy is an asset. However, be careful not to compromise too much at the expense of your values.

protector.title: The Protector
protector.desc: You defend the weak with a big heart. You are empathetic and loyal.
protector.advice: Your empathy is a superpower. Remember to set boundaries to protect yourself too.

survivor.title: The Survivor
survivor.desc: You focus on ensuring your own safety. You avoid risks and conflicts.
survivor.advice: Self-protection is human. However, consider what the cost of silence is in the long run.

steps.title: Shadow of a Star
steps.text: You are a marketing specialist. Your team's 'Star Performer', Alex, brings in huge revenue, but has a habit of embarrassing the new intern, Eva, with subtle jabs in meetings. Today Alex said to Eva: 'Maybe this industry just isn't for you', and Eva left crying.
steps.question: What do you do?

options.text: Intervene immediately and publicly: 'Alex, that was inappropriate.'
Wait for the meeting to end and speak to Alex privately.
Go after Eva to comfort her.
Stay silent. Alex is too influential to oppose.

steps.title: Pressure from Above
steps.text: Alex heard that Eva's crying attracted attention. Your manager calls you into the office. 'Alex is vital to us right now. Eva is... sensitive. I hope you support team unity and don't spread stories.'
steps.question: How do you reply?

options.text: I understand. I'll just focus on my work.
I cannot accept bullying, regardless of results.
I understand the pressure, but supporting Eva helps results in the long run.
If Eva leaves because of this, I will tell everyone why.

steps.title: Escalation
steps.text: A week later, Eva is on sick leave. Alex jokes in the break room: 'The weak crumble on the road of life'. Others laugh uncomfortably.
steps.question: This is a decisive moment. What do you do?

options.text: Contact the occupational safety representative on Eva's behalf.
Laugh along to avoid conflict.
Say out loud: 'That is not funny, it is cruel.'
Suggest a team meeting about rules without naming names.

organization_resources.title: Organizational Resources & Support
organization_resources.subtitle: Tools and materials for managers and leadership

resources.title: Identify Risks (Checklist)
resources.description: List of early warning signs in the team.

content.item1: Silent Approval: If inappropriate behavior is not addressed immediately, it becomes the norm in three months.
content.item2: Cliques: Splitting the team into 'us' and 'them' is often the first step towards systematic exclusion.
content.item3: Withholding Information: When information is used as a tool of power, trust erodes and cover-ups begin.
content.item4: Scapegoating: Blaming one person for common problems is a classic group dynamic defense mechanism.
content.item5: Constant Criticism: If feedback is directed at the person rather than the work, it is no longer management but harassment.

resources.title: Financial Impact
resources.description: Calculations and facts to support decision making.

content.item1: Sick Leave: A bullied employee is absent on average 7-15 days more per year than others.
content.item2: Turnover: Recruiting and onboarding a new expert often costs 50-150% of the annual salary.
content.item3: Decreased Efficiency: Presenteeism (at work but not present) can reduce team efficiency by up to 30%.
content.item4: Legal Risks: Reputational damage and potential compensation can rise to tens of thousands of euros.
content.item5: Innovation Loss: In an atmosphere of fear, no one dares to suggest new things or question the old.

content.item1: Meeting Situation: When someone is run over or humiliated publicly, intervene immediately. 'Let's take that again.'
content.item2: Coffee Break: When gossip starts, change the subject or leave. Body language is a strong message.
content.item3: Email: If the tone is inappropriate, do not reply in kind. Request a face-to-face discussion.
content.item4: Onboarding: State right at the beginning what behavior is expected and what is not tolerated.
content.item5: Feedback Discussion: Focus on facts and observations, not assumptions or personality.

toxic_star.title: 1. 'Toxic Star' Dilemma
toxic_star.matrix_desc: Harvard study (Housman & Minor, 2015) shows: One "toxic star" costs the company 2x more than they produce. Assess your team members with this tool.

analysis.toxic: TOXIC STAR: Destroys team morale. Turnover costs more than their results.
analysis.star: STAR: True top performer. Hold on to them!
analysis.potential: POTENTIAL: Needs support for results, but attitude is right.
analysis.underperformer: UNDERPERFORMER: Wrong recruitment or wrong role.

toxic_star.conclusion: Conclusion: A manager has a duty to intervene even with "stars". If you let toxic behavior continue in the name of results, you drive five other experts out of the house.

legal.title: 2. Legal Backbone
legal.content_title: The Law is on Your Side

law.title: Occupational Safety Act 28 §
law.text: "The employer must, after becoming aware of harassment, take action with available means to remove the grievance."

right.title: Right to Direct
right.text: The manager has the right and duty to define what is acceptable behavior. You don't need consensus to intervene.

legal.quote: "You are not mean when you intervene – you are professional and following the law."

conflict.title: 3. Avoiding Conflict
conflict.desc: According to studies, "Laissez-faire" (let it go) leadership is most stressful for employees. Non-intervention is an active act.
conflict.exercise_title: Exposure Exercise: Say it Out Loud
conflict.exercise_desc: Read the sentences out loud. If your heart rate rises, repeat until it stabilizes.
sentences: I noticed in the meeting yesterday that you interrupted Lisa three times.
This behavior does not align with our values, and it must stop.
I want to discuss your way of giving feedback.
conflict.action: I am ready to speak directly

restorative.title: 4. Restorative Justice
restorative.intro: A bullying case doesn't end with a warning. The team is often traumatized and the position of "scapegoat" is open.

steps.title: 1. Restore Trust
steps.text: Speak to the team generally about what happened (no names), but confirm that the process has been handled and norms clarified.

steps.title: 2. Protect the Victim from Labeling
steps.text: Ensure the reporter is not left alone or treated as a "snitch". Monitor the situation actively for 3 months.

accountability.title: 5. Accountability & Support
accountability.desc: The organization's immune system strengthens only if management dares to act. You have support, law, and justification on your side.

reward.title: Rewarding
reward.text: Psychological safety is a result metric. Good atmosphere is rewarded.

support.title: Support Network
support.text: Direct line to HR. Don't stay alone with difficult cases.

ui.tip_text: Studies show that confident boundary setting reduces bullying situations by up to 50%. Documentation gives credibility to interveners.
ui.psych_text: Use "I-statements" ("I feel...") to remove aggression while maintaining your space.
ui.neuro_text: For neurodivergent individuals, visual documentation (screenshots, photos of spaces) can be easier way to structure events than just text. In board work, clear written rules create needed predictability.

association_basics.speaker: Narrator
association_basics.text: You are on the board of a hobby association. You notice strange dynamics in the WhatsApp group: The Chair and a couple of others make decisions past others and joke at others' expense.

choices.text: Start documenting events in the evidence vault
choices.feedback: Wise. Facts help you stay in reality even if others try to downplay it.

choices.text: Ask in the group: "How was this decision made?"
choices.feedback: A direct question forces the clique to explain their actions publicly.

association_basics.speaker: Narrator
association_basics.text: You open the evidence vault. The Chair writes: "Me and Tero decided to move the event. You others can handle the load-in."

choices.text: Log: "Chair and Tero decided past the board on 12.05."
choices.feedback: Documentation turns a subjective feeling into objective evidence.

association_basics.speaker: Chair
association_basics.text: Chair: "Well, me and Tero just quickly looked at this to get it out of the way. No need to make a fuss, we're friends right! 😉"

choices.text: Use a warning phrase: "Following rules is in everyone's interest."
choices.feedback: Warning Phrases are short and matter-of-fact. They stop manipulation.

association_basics.speaker: Narrator
association_basics.text: You now have a list of situations where rules were broken. You decide to bring it up in the next meeting with allies.

choices.text: Finish Exercise
choices.feedback: Great! Gathering information is the first step to change.

association_basics.speaker: Narrator

choices.text: Finish Exercise

hobby_boundaries.speaker: Narrator
hobby_boundaries.text: In your hobby group, one member constantly "jokes" at your expense in front of others. It feels bad, but others just laugh along.

choices.text: Use an I-message immediately in the situation
choices.feedback: An I-message ("I feel...") is according to studies the most effective way to set a boundary without attacking back.

choices.text: Swallow your anger and try to laugh along
choices.feedback: Silence is often interpreted as acceptance. This consumes your resources.

hobby_boundaries.speaker: You
hobby_boundaries.text: "I feel uncomfortable when you make jokes about my performance in front of others. I would hope you stop that."

choices.text: Wait for the answer calmly
choices.feedback: Calm waiting shows you stand behind your words.

hobby_boundaries.speaker: Other Member
hobby_boundaries.text: "Oh, I didn't mean anything bad... sorry if you took it that way. I won't do it anymore."

choices.text: Thank them for honesty and continue hobby
choices.feedback: Great! Your self-esteem grew and you set a clear boundary.

hobby_boundaries.speaker: Narrator

choices.text: Stop the situation now: "This is not funny anymore."

choices.text: Quit the hobby in silence
choices.feedback: Escape is a solution, but it leaves wounds and the bully moves to the next target.

Why does exclusion
hurt?
intro.text: For the brain, social rejection is the same as physical pain. It activates the same areas in the brain. That's why 'don't care' advice doesn't work.

survival.title: Survival Kit
survival.text: When you feel sidelined, try these three steps.

step1.title: 1. Acknowledge the pain
step1.text: Say to yourself: 'This hurts because I am human.' Pain tells you that you need connection.

step2.title: 2. Find connection elsewhere
step2.text: Send a message to a friend. Make eye contact with a cashier. Even a small accepting look relieves pain.

step3.title: 3. Validate yourself

boundaries_module.subtitle: Reclaiming Your Space

intro.title:
Boundaries are not walls.
They are gateways.
intro.text:
In a bullying situation, your boundaries have often been trampled down. For recovery, it's important to learn to say "no" again, so you can say "yes" to your own well-being.

A boundary is not an attack on another, but an act of love toward yourself.

categories_step.title: Which boundary do you need most?

professional.title: Professional Boundaries
professional.description: What you do and when. Limits of responsibility.
examples: I don't respond to emails after 5 PM.
This task is not part of my job description right now.
I need 3 hours of uninterrupted time daily.

emotional.title: Emotional Boundaries
emotional.description: Whose burden you carry and where you spend your energy.
examples: I can't listen to this right now, I don't have the space.
I don't need to explain my decisions to you.
I can discuss this professionally, but I won't accept yelling.

physical.title: Physical & Communication Boundaries
physical.description: Your space, touch, and how you're approached.
examples: I'd prefer we don't use personal channels for work matters.
I'd appreciate if you kept a bit of distance when speaking.

boundaries.text: Heroics don't help if you burn out yourself. Remember the safety checklist:

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: You see your colleague Marja being criticized baselessly and sarcastically in a team meeting. Marja looks paralyzed and stares at the table.

choices.text: Move to sit next to Marja and ask quietly: 'Are you okay?'
choices.feedback: Research: Mere physical presence and asking 'Are you okay?' reduces the victim's anxiety by up to 40%.

choices.text: Challenge the bully directly in the meeting: 'Stop that immediately!'
choices.feedback: Direct confrontation can escalate and increase your own risk, although it is brave.

steps.speaker: Marja
steps.text: Marja glances at you gratefully and takes a deep breath. The bully slows down their speech noticing that Marja is no longer alone.

choices.text: Name the situation factually: 'Shall we continue with the agenda? Marja's input was important here.'
choices.feedback: Showing solidarity publicly stabilizes the situation without a fight.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The bully turns to you: 'Well look, someone's being sensitive today! Do you have a club going on?' The atmosphere tightens.

choices.text: Stay calm: 'It's about workplace rules, not sensitivity.'
choices.feedback: Calmness is the best weapon when the other party tries to personalize the conflict.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The meeting ends. Marja comes to thank you later. She says that without your support she might have burst into tears or left the room.

choices.text: Finish exercise
choices.feedback: Great! You are an active witness breaking the cycle of isolation.

steps.speaker: WhatsApp Group
steps.text: Mocking memes about the newest hobbyist start spreading in the group. No one comments anything, although 20 people have seen the messages.

choices.text: Write in the group: 'This doesn't belong here, do others agree?'
choices.feedback: By asking for others' opinion, you break 'pluralistic ignorance' and share responsibility.

choices.text: Leave the group in silence
choices.feedback: Leaving is a sign, but it leaves the victim alone. Try intervening in the group.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: It's quiet for a moment, but then two other members thumbs-up your message and write: 'True, let's stick to the topic.' The Bystander Effect breaks.

choices.text: Suggest reviewing the rules to the admin
choices.feedback: Structural intervention (rules) prevents recurrence.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: You are out of the group, but you know the mocking continues. You feel guilty and detached from the community.

choices.text: Send private message to victim: 'I saw the messages, they are not ok.'
choices.feedback: Even if you didn't intervene publicly, private support is vital for the victim.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Your action encouraged others to intervene too. The group culture is now clearer and safer for everyone. You have broken pluralistic ignorance.

choices.text: Finish exercise
choices.feedback: An active bystander is the backbone of a healthy community. When one speaks, 'silent disapproval' turns into collective action.

intro.title:
Bullying is an
expensive choice.
intro.text:
Zero tolerance is often just a word. When we turn the malaise associated with bullying into numbers, it becomes a strategic risk that management is forced to address.

Let's calculate what an 'unquestionable culture' costs your organization annually.

result.title: Bullying costs {{amount}}€ per year.
result.subtitle: Estimate is based on {{count}} affected employees.
result.box1_text: This calculation implies no reputational damage or potential legal costs, which can easily double the sum. Presenteeism (employee is present but efficiency has dropped) is often an invisible 'leak' consuming thousands of euros a month.
result.box2_text: An intervention that reduces bullying by only 20% pays for itself with {{savings}}€ savings in the first year alone. Cultural change is not just humanity, it is a productivity leap.

culture_thermometer.title: Culture Thermometer
culture_thermometer.subtitle: Organization Health Check

intro.title:
What kind of air
do you breathe?
intro.text:
Culture doesn't change with posters, but with daily actions and a sense of safety. This thermometer measures psychological safety and structural protection anonymously.

Answer honestly based on current status.

questions: I can raise concerns about workplace behavior without fear of negative consequences for myself.
My supervisor reacts consistently when someone behaves inappropriately.
In our team, difficult issues can be discussed openly without a norm of silence.
I feel I am treated fairly in task distribution and feedback.
I clearly know how to report bullying suspicions and I trust the process.
I have seen a situation (within 12 months) where inappropriate behavior was addressed quickly.
There are no 'untouchable' people in our team due to their position.
If I made a mistake, I wouldn't expect to be humiliated or isolated.
In my workplace, there is a clear difference between firm feedback and bullying.
Management's actions show that bullying has real consequences.
Employees are recruited and promoted fairly, not based on personal relationships.
I have received clear information about acceptable and unacceptable behavior in the workplace.
At our workplace, newcomers are welcomed and integrated regardless of their background.
Workplace conflicts are addressed constructively, not swept under the rug.
I feel I can be honest about workload and stress without being seen as weak.
Our team has regular conversations about well-being and culture.
I have observed that all employees are treated with equal respect regardless of their role.
I trust that HR and management actually follow through on reported issues.
The atmosphere at work allows me to relax and bring my best performance.
Our organization has clear, written anti-bullying policies that everyone knows.

result.title: State of Culture
result.safety_desc: This figure tells how freely employees dare to be themselves and raise issues without fear of humiliation or retaliation.
result.risk_desc: This figure describes the credibility of management, processes, and intervention. The higher the number, the harder it is for bullying to take root in structures.
result.critical: Measurement shows critical deficiencies in either sense of safety or structures. This state exposes the organization to prolonged bullying cases and expensive turnover.
result.strong: Your organization has a strong foundation. Continue open dialogue and ensure no 'untouchable' favorites are created through the LMX phenomenon.

intro.title: Leadership Blind Spots
intro.text:
The manager is the gatekeeper: your choices in decisive moments either cut off bullying or make it part of everyday life.

Test your ability to identify and intervene in three decisive moments.

scenarios.title: Decisive Moment 1: First Signal
scenarios.description: In a team meeting, you notice a 'joke' that clearly confuses and silences one member. Others laugh.
scenarios.choiceA: Stop it: Address it clearly immediately or right after: 'I noticed this, I want to ensure it doesn't happen again.'
scenarios.choiceB: Ignore: 'It's just their humor,' you think. If I intervene, I ruin the good mood.
scenarios.feedbackA: Correct. By stopping even small things, you signal that laughing at someone's expense is not part of the culture.
scenarios.feedbackB: Risky. Inaction normalizes the behavior and signals that this kind of game is part of the deal.

scenarios.title: Decisive Moment 2: Official Report
scenarios.description: An employee comes to you and says: 'I feel like I'm being treated inappropriately.'
scenarios.choiceA: Take seriously: Thank them for their trust, document, explain the process, and agree on a timeline for investigation.
scenarios.choiceB: Downplay: 'You might be a bit sensitive, you know Lisa just has that style.'
scenarios.feedbackA: Great. The psychological contract is maintained when the organization responds as promised and appropriately.
scenarios.feedbackB: Dangerous. The reporter feels left alone and the threshold to tell in the future grows. The psychological contract breaks.

scenarios.title: Decisive Moment 3: Follow-up
scenarios.description: The matter has been clarified and boundaries agreed upon. Weeks have passed and the situation seems to have calmed down on the surface.
scenarios.choiceA: Active monitoring: Ensure agreed actions, keep regular check-ins with both parties.
scenarios.choiceB: Assumption: You assume the matter is over because no one comes to complain anymore.
scenarios.feedbackA: Essential. Bullies often just change target or tactic. Continuous monitoring guarantees change.
scenarios.feedbackB: Error. Silence does not mean a solution. Often it just means giving up or fear of reporting again.

items.title: React (Signal)
items.desc: Do not belittle even the smallest inappropriateness. It is a seed that takes root if watered by silence.

items.title: Register (Report)
items.desc: Document everything. Objective data is a manager's best friend when things start to be unraveled.

items.title: Resolve & Monitor
items.desc: Ensure actions bite. Monitor at 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months. Bullying is removed only with persistence.

analysis_steps.title: What is the risk?
analysis_steps.desc: Direct intervention can increase risk if you are unsure of safety.

analysis_steps.title: What is the goal?
analysis_steps.desc: The most important thing is to break the isolation and show support.

empathy.title: Mirror Neuron Rescue
empathy.subtitle: Experience the situation through another's eyes

steps.speaker: Matt
steps.text: You are in the break room. You hear three colleagues laughing at Janne's new idea across the room. Janne sits alone at a table staring at his coffee cup.

choices.text: Go sit next to Janne and start chatting about something else.
choices.feedback: Good! You broke the isolation.

choices.text: Shout at the group: 'Stop that trash talk!'
choices.feedback: Brave, but you escalated the situation.

choices.text: Continue drinking coffee so you don't become a target yourself.
choices.feedback: You protected yourself, but Janne was left alone.

steps.speaker: Janne
steps.text: Thanks for coming. It felt a bit... weird to be alone.

choices.text: Of course. Their behavior was inappropriate.

steps.speaker: Group
steps.text: The group falls silent and stares at you angrily. Janne looks uncomfortable.

choices.text: Go to Janne anyway.

steps.speaker: You
steps.text: You leave. You feel a sting in your heart as you see Janne left alone.

choices.text: Try again later.

intro.title: Are you a silent witness?
intro.text:
Most workplace bullying happens in front of others. The bystander's reaction – or lack thereof – determines if bullying continues.

In this module, you will learn 5 safe ways to intervene.

questions.scenario: In a team meeting, the manager sighs heavily and rolls their eyes whenever Matt speaks. Others start snickering.
questions.explanation: Repeated, non-verbal humiliation and creating peer pressure is bullying, not 'humor'.

questions.scenario: A colleague disagrees with the project direction and argues their point strongly but professionally in a meeting.
questions.explanation: Disagreeing and debating are part of work, as long as it doesn't get personal.

questions.scenario: A colleague consistently 'forgets' to invite Lisa to lunch and team coffees, even though everyone else is invited.
questions.explanation: Social exclusion (ostracism) is one of the most common and damaging forms of bullying.

responsibility.title: Bystander Effect & Responsibility
responsibility.text: See what happens to the probability of intervening when there are more witnesses.
responsibility.explanation_alone: When you are the only witness, you feel 100% responsibility and are likely to act.
responsibility.explanation_group: The more people there are, the more we assume 'someone else' will handle it. This is called diffusion of responsibility.

cheat_sheet.title: Delegate
cheat_sheet.desc: Ask for help from others or a manager.

cheat_sheet.title: Delay
cheat_sheet.desc: Support the victim after the situation.

scenario.speaker: Situation
scenario.text: You are in the break room. You hear two colleagues talking loudly: "Did you hear what the new guy messed up again? Unbelievable incompetence." The new employee sits at the next table and hears everything.

choices.text: Go sit next to the new employee and ask: "Hey, how is your project going?"
choices.feedback: Great! You distracted attention from the bullies (Distract) and offered support without confrontation. This is often the safest way.

choices.text: Say loudly: "Hey, we don't talk about colleagues like that."
choices.feedback: Brave! Direct intervention makes the boundary clear. However, always assess your safety before confrontation.

choices.text: Go to the new employee later: "I'm sorry about their behavior, it wasn't cool."
choices.feedback: Important! Delayed support (Delay) is vital. It removes the victim's doubt that they might have imagined the situation.

scenario.speaker: Narrator
scenario.text: The new employee smiles with relief and starts chatting with you. The bullies go quiet for a moment and then change the subject as the 'audience' disappeared.

choices.text: Continue

scenario.speaker: Narrator
scenario.text: The room goes silent. One of the speakers mumbles "it was just a joke", but the conversation stops. The new employee gives you a grateful look.

choices.text: Continue

scenario.speaker: Narrator
scenario.text: The new employee sighs: "Thanks for saying that. I thought I imagined it all." You validated their experience, which is critical for recovery.

choices.text: Continue

boundaries.title: Before You Intervene...
boundaries.text: Heroics don't help if you burn out yourself. Remember the safety checklist:
checklist: Do I have power/status in this situation?
Can I make the situation worse by intervening now?

intro.title:
It's not character.
It's biology.
intro.text:
When you switch your brain to 'war mode' for a long time, it starts to change. The same mechanisms that once saved you now prevent focus and joy.

Good news? The brain is plastic (neuroplasticity). We can 'rewire' it for safety.

amygdala.title: Amygdala
amygdala.desc_text: Constantly scans for threats. After trauma, it's hyperactive – screaming 'DANGER!' even if you sit safely at home.

prefrontal.title: Prefrontal Cortex
prefrontal.desc_text: Responsible for logic, regulating emotions, and making decisions. Under stress, this part 'shuts down' so energy goes to pure survival.

hijack.title: Amygdala Hijack
hijack.text: When stress levels rise too high, your wisest part loses control.
hijack.btn_breathe: Breathe: Return control to the ruler
hijack.btn_stress: Stress: Let the amygdala take over
hijack.quote: You are not stupid or insecure – your brain is just saving energy for survival.

repair.title: Rewiring
repair.text: Your brain changes based on what you practice. Every day.

item1.title: Name the feeling
item1.text: When you say 'I am scared', you activate the prefrontal cortex and the amygdala's scream fades.

item2.title: Somatic work
item2.text: Calming the body (like shaking) sends a message to the brain: 'The danger is over'.

item3.title: Small wins
item3.text: Your brain needs evidence of safety. Do one small, manageable thing at a time.

summary.title: Recovery has begun.
summary.text: Your brain has done its best to protect you. Now it's time to teach it that it can rest. Be patient – growing connections takes time, but it happens with every repetition.

intro.title: Why does the body remember?
intro.text: Trauma and chronic stress are not just 'in your head'. They are stored in the body as tension, vigilance, or numbness. For the mind to calm down, the body must first feel safe.

shake.title: The Shake
shake.desc: Release adrenaline by shaking the body.

steps.text: Stand up if you can.
Start by shaking your hands.
Include your shoulders.
Shake your whole body.
steps.instruction: Like a dog getting out of water.

steps.text: Stop and feel the flow.

breath.title: Box Breathing
breath.desc: Lower heart rate with rhythmic breathing.

steps.text: Breathe in...
Hold...
Breathe out...
Hold...

ground.title: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding
ground.desc: Bring your mind to the present using senses.

steps.text: Find 5 things you see.
Find 4 things you can touch.
steps.instruction: Feel the texture with your fingers.

steps.text: Find 3 sounds you hear.
Find 2 things you smell.
Find 1 thing you can taste.
steps.instruction: Or feel the taste in your mouth.

steps.text: Clench your fists...
And let go completely.
Pull your shoulders to your ears...
Drop your shoulders down.
Squeeze your eyes shut tight...
Let your face melt into relaxation.

debrief.title: How does your body feel now?
debrief.text: Even a small moment of nervous system calming helps recovery. You can return to this whenever you feel hyper-alert or numb.

intro.title:
Safety
Restoration
intro.text: Trauma and prolonged stress tune the nervous system to a constant state of alarm. In this exercise, we learn to calm the body and identify safe havens.

grounding.title: Grounding
grounding.text: When anxiety strikes, bring attention to the present moment with the 5-4-3-2-1 technique. Try this now.

items.text: things you see around you
things you can touch
things you hear
things you can smell
thing you can taste

anchors.title: Safety Anchors
anchors.text: List places and people with whom you are completely safe.

summary.title: Exercise Completed!
summary.text:
You have created a safety plan for yourself.
Remember: Safety is not just a place, it is a state in your nervous system.
summary.hint: Return to these in your mind whenever you feel threatened.

action_protocols.title: Response Toolkit
action_protocols.subtitle: Concrete Action Models
action_protocols.description: Don't freeze. Here are ready-made words and plans, so you know exactly what to do.

acute_scripts.intro_text:
Three steps to manage chaos.
1. Stop: Pause your reaction (breathe).
2. Speak: Set the boundary.
3. Document: Write it down immediately.

public_mockery.title: Public Mockery
public_mockery.script: I do not like this comment. Stop it immediately.
public_mockery.nuance: Calm, low voice. No smiling. Eye contact.

withholding_info.title: Withholding Info
withholding_info.script: I need this information for my work. Send it now.
withholding_info.nuance: Don't ask 'could you'. State the need. CC a representative if repeated.
withholding_info.next: Screenshot your request. if no answer, send reminder.

isolation.title: Isolation
isolation.script: Why wasn't I invited? Add me in the future.
isolation.nuance: Ask directly in a meeting or chat. Make the invisible visible.
isolation.next: Ask the team: 'Did you notice I was missing?'

difficult_conversation.title: Difficult Conversation Formula
difficult_conversation.intro: Use this 5-step framework in a private discussion.

steps.title: 1. Opening
steps.script: Thank you for coming. I want to discuss our interaction. This is important for my work.
steps.tip: Frame neutrally. Don't blame, invite to discuss.

steps.title: 2. Concrete Example
steps.script: In last Tuesday's meeting you said publicly 'You don't get this'. I experience this as dismissive. How does that sound to you?
steps.tip: State fact (what happened) and impact (how it felt). End with open question.

steps.title: 3. Boundary
steps.script: In the future, I expect the snide remarks to stop. My work flows best without it. Do you agree?
steps.tip: State clear requirement. Don't ask for permission, but commitment.

steps.title: 4. Follow-up & Support
steps.script: How do we ensure this doesn't repeat? Do I need anything from you?
steps.tip: Share responsibility for the solution. 'How do we succeed in this?'

steps.title: 5. Closing & Documentation
steps.script: Thanks for the talk. I'll note this down. Anything to add?
steps.tip: Make it official. Send a memo by email (CC representative).

manager_chain.title: Manager is the Bully?
manager_chain.intro: When power is misused, you must protect yourself with bureaucracy. Don't wait. Document everything.

steps.script: I find [action] inappropriate. I ask you to stop.
I am reporting [Undisputable facts]. I need a clarification.
I need help resolving this. Attached: documentation.
Bullying causes symptoms. I request a statement on work capacity.
Employer has not taken action despite notification.

safety_plan.title: My Safety Plan
safety_plan.intro: Fill this out and save a screenshot on your phone.

form.reaction_placeholder: E.g. I leave the room for 5 mins.
form.phrase_value: I am using my safety plan now – I need help.
form.exit_placeholder: E.g. If no change in 3 weeks -> Sick leave.
form.place_placeholder: E.g. Cafe at lunch / Remote work.
form.disclaimer: Data is not saved on server for privacy. Take a screenshot.

exit_strategy.title: Exit Strategy
exit_strategy.subtitle: When is it time to leave?

intro.title:
When is it time to
Leave?
intro.text: Leaving is not giving up. It is sometimes the only correct strategic move to protect your health. This tool helps you assess the situation objectively.

signs.title: Early Warning Signs
signs.subtitle: Select all that you recognize in your situation.

list.repetition: Repetition: Situations repeat weekly and are not random.
list.exclusion: Exclusion: I am repeatedly left out of information or invites.
list.health: Health: I experience physical symptoms (stomach pain, insomnia) when thinking about work.
list.normalization: Normalization: Inappropriate behavior is dismissed as 'humor' or 'house style'.
list.target: Targeting: Criticism is directed at me personally, not my work.

manager_test.title: Manager Test
manager_test.subtitle: How has the manager or management reacted to the situation?

questions.text: Manager intervened within a week of notification.
Manager listened to both parties equally.
A clear written plan with follow-up was made.
Manager belittled the situation or advised to 'ignore it'.
Retaliation or pressure occurred after notification.

manager_test.insight: Did you know? Studies show intervention fails in 60-80% of cases if management is passive. Management support is critical.

traffic_light.title: Your Assessment
traffic_light.subtitle: Based on the signs you observed and management action.

red.desc: Signs indicate the situation is dangerous to health and no change is in sight.

yellow.desc: The situation is worrying. Active monitoring and Plan B are needed.

green.desc: There are still opportunities for corrective moves, but be vigilant.

stat_box.title: Statistical Fact:
stat_box.text: People typically leave within 6-12 months when health starts to fail. Don't wait for burnout.

plan.title: Action Plan
plan.subtitle: Take control. Here is a proposal for next steps.

section1.title: Secure Your Back
items: Visit occupational health to document symptoms.

section2.title: Mental Detachment
items: Focus on leisure and identity outside work.
Define a 'backdoor' (e.g. study leave or savings).

target_date.title: Target Date
target_date.text: Set a deadline for yourself. If the situation hasn't improved by then, fully activate Plan B.

intro.title:
Return home.
To your own body.
intro.text: When the mind races or feels numb, grounding returns you to this moment. It is not about removing thoughts, but shifting attention to where you are safe: the now.

exercises_view.title: Small moments of presence
exercises_view.quote: "Grounding is a skill that strengthens with every repetition."

observation.title: Conscious Observation
observation.description: Choose one object and study it as if seeing it for the first time.
observation.content_intro: Pick up or look at an object in front of you. Notice:
steps: How does light reflect off its surface?
If you named three different color shades in it, what are they?
observation.hint: This exercise interrupts automatic thought chains by anchoring the mind to the present.

sound.title: Soundscape
sound.description: Close your eyes and find the farthest sound you can hear.
sound.content_intro: Stop and listen. Do not name sounds, just listen to them as waves:
steps: What is a sound coming from outside your current space?
Do you hear your own breath or the rustle of clothes?
What happens in the silence between sounds?

anchor.title: Safety Anchor
anchor.description: Find a physical touch point that reminds you of safety.
anchor.content_intro: Press palms together or place hand on heart. Feel:
steps: The warmth of your hand against your skin.
Say in your mind: "I am here, in this moment it is safe."

summary.title: Be kind to yourself.
summary.text: These exercises are always with you. You can do them on the bus, in a meeting, or just before bed. Every time you anchor yourself, you teach your nervous system that there is space to rest in this moment.

intro.title:
Brain stuck?
It's the rumination network.
intro.text:
When we do nothing, the "Default Mode Network" (DMN) activates in our brains. After trauma, it turns into rumination: an endless chain of past wrongs and future fears.

It is not thinking. It is the brain's way of trying to solve the impossible.

explanation.title: DMN: "The Worrier of Yesterday"

rest_illusion.title: Illusion of Rest
rest_illusion.text: DMN activates when the "focused network" shuts down. After trauma, the brain doesn't know how to rest, instead it starts replaying traumatic memories trying to find a solution.

loop.title: The Loop
loop.text: Rumination is like running in circles in a forest: you are active but getting nowhere. This consumes huge amounts of energy and prevents recovery.

explanation.action: See what the loop looks like

simulation.title: Cycle of Rumination
simulation.subtitle: Your brain repeats these phrases thousands of times a day.
phrases: What if I had done differently?
simulation.hint: "Recognize that this is your brain's automatic loop."

breakout.title: How to stop the DMN?
breakout.subtitle: Rumination only stops by changing the state.

tools.title: Focused Sense
tools.text: The brain cannot ruminate and focus on senses at the same time. Feel your soles on the ground or touch a surface.

tools.title: Name the Loop
tools.text: Say to yourself: 'Now my brain is ruminating again.' This specificies control to the prefrontal cortex.

tools.title: Concrete Action
tools.text: Do something physical. Clean a shelf, walk across the room, open a window. Change the environment.

summary.title: The cycle is broken.
summary.text: Your brain tried to protect you by worrying, but now you know it leads nowhere. Choose conscious focus instead of rumination whenever you notice the loop starting.

difficult_conversations.title: Difficult Conversations
difficult_conversations.subtitle: Choose an opponent and practice setting boundaries safely.

ui.won_desc: You maintained your professionalism and boundaries.
ui.lost_desc: Emotions took over or you gave up your boundaries.

aggro.title: The Aggressor
aggro.intro: LISTEN TO ME! Why is this report late?! Are you completely incompetent??

dialogs.opponent: This is total bulls**t! I can't believe we pay you a salary!

options.text: Sorry, I try my best...
options.reply: Trying isn't enough! Do your job!

options.text: Do not speak to me like that.
options.reply: I speak how I want when there are no results!

options.text: We will discuss when you calm down. Inappropriate behavior does not help.

victim.title: The Victim
victim.intro: Why do you always persecute me? I've had it so hard...

dialogs.opponent: Don't I ever do anything right in your opinion? *sob*

options.text: No, you don't do wrong, you see...
options.reply: You always explain! You hate me!

options.text: We are discussing the task, not you as a person.
Stop that crying.

gaslight.title: The Gaslighter
gaslight.intro: What are you talking about? I never promised that. Are you imagining things again?

dialogs.opponent: You have a vivid imagination. Are you stressed?

options.text: Maybe I am... do I remember wrong?
I have an email with the date.
options.reply: Emails can be faked or misinterpreted.

options.text: The fact is this. I discuss documents, not memories.
options.reply: You are so uptight... but fine.

intro.title: Why do good people do nothing?
intro.text:
Have you ever seen bullying and frozen? It's not because you are a coward.

It is the Bystander Effect, a psychological phenomenon that prevents helping in group situations. Once you understand the mechanism, you can break it.

diffusion.title: Diffusion of Responsibility
diffusion.subtitle: "Someone else will handle it."
diffusion.explanation: When you are alone, you know help depends on you. In a large group, we subconsciously assume someone else is more qualified or ready to act.

evaluation.title: Evaluation Apprehension
evaluation.subtitle: "What if I mess up?"

pressure.title: Audience Pressure
pressure.text: We fear overreacting. What if it was just a joke? What if others think I'm difficult?

risk.title: Social Risks
risk.text: At work, we fear loss of status or being labeled a 'snitch'. This is a natural, evolutionary defense mechanism.

evaluation.solution: 💡 Solution: Lower the threshold. Intervening doesn't have to be heroic. A small distraction or question is enough.

ignorance.title: Pluralistic Ignorance
ignorance.subtitle: "No one else is reacting, so there is no emergency."

reveal_shown.title: Everyone is uncertain.
reveal_shown.text: Everyone looks at others' "calm" expressions and thinks they are the only one worried. In reality, everyone is just trying to hide their fear.

steps.title: Recognize the phenomenon
steps.text: When you notice hesitation, remember: "This is just the bystander effect."

steps.title: Act first
steps.text: Even one voiced concern breaks pluralistic ignorance. Others will follow.

intro.title: It's not your memory.
intro.text:
Gaslighting is manipulation aimed at making the target doubt their own perception, memory, or sanity.

It is a subtle process that erodes self-esteem piece by piece. But when you learn to recognize the code, it loses its power.

tactics.title: What they say vs. What happens
tactics.subtitle: Click cards to see behind the scenes.

items.phrase: You are way too sensitive, it was just a joke.
items.translation: They try to minimize your experience and shift focus away from their action.
items.description: Makes your feelings 'wrong', causing you to doubt your own reactions.

items.phrase: That never happened. You remember wrong.
items.translation: They lie directly to change the course of history.
items.description: The most dangerous form. When repeated enough, you start trusting their memory instead of yours.

items.phrase: Why do you always start a fight? You clearly have issues.
items.translation: They make you the problem to avoid responsibility.
items.description: Changes the subject by attacking your character ('ad hominem').

stages.title: Descent into Fog
stages.subtitle: Gaslighting doesn't happen at once, it is a slow process.

items.name: Disbelief
items.text: You think they must be mistaken or confused. You don't take it personally yet.

items.name: Defense
items.text: You try to argue and prove you are right. You use huge energy defending yourself.

items.name: Depression
items.text: You start believing you are the broken one. You doubt every thought and feeling.

reclaim.title: Reclaim Reality
reclaim.subtitle: Manipulation breaks when examined in light.

items.title: Write things down immediately
items.text: Phrases, times, and your own feelings. Documentation is an anchor that keeps you in reality.

items.title: Trust 'reality checkers'
items.text: Talk to friends or colleagues who know you. They help you see you are not going crazy.

items.title: Stop arguing
items.text: The Gaslighter will not apologize. The most important thing is that YOU know the truth. You don't need to prove it to them.

summary.title: Truth is strong.
summary.text: Now that you know these tactics, you are a harder target. Do not let anyone write your history for you. Your perception is valuable and true.

idealist.title: The Idealist
idealist.desc: You place justice above all. You are brave, but may get into conflicts that jeopardize your own position.
idealist.advice: Your courage is admirable. However, remember to choose your battles so you don't burn out.

pragmatist.title: The Pragmatist
pragmatist.desc: You look for solutions that work in practice. You try to balance results and people.
pragmatist.advice: Your diplomacy is an asset. However, be careful not to compromise too much at the expense of your values.

protector.title: The Protector
protector.desc: You defend the weak with a big heart. You are empathetic and loyal.
protector.advice: Your empathy is a superpower. Remember to set boundaries to protect yourself too.

survivor.title: The Survivor
survivor.desc: You focus on ensuring your own safety. You avoid risks and conflicts.
survivor.advice: Self-protection is human. However, consider what the cost of silence is in the long run.

steps.title: Shadow of a Star
steps.text: You are a marketing specialist. Your team's 'Star Performer', Alex, brings in huge revenue, but has a habit of embarrassing the new intern, Eva, with subtle jabs in meetings. Today Alex said to Eva: 'Maybe this industry just isn't for you', and Eva left crying.
steps.question: What do you do?

options.text: Intervene immediately and publicly: 'Alex, that was inappropriate.'
Wait for the meeting to end and speak to Alex privately.
Go after Eva to comfort her.
Stay silent. Alex is too influential to oppose.

steps.title: Pressure from Above
steps.text: Alex heard that Eva's crying attracted attention. Your manager calls you into the office. 'Alex is vital to us right now. Eva is... sensitive. I hope you support team unity and don't spread stories.'
steps.question: How do you reply?

options.text: I understand. I'll just focus on my work.
I cannot accept bullying, regardless of results.
I understand the pressure, but supporting Eva helps results in the long run.
If Eva leaves because of this, I will tell everyone why.

steps.title: Escalation
steps.text: A week later, Eva is on sick leave. Alex jokes in the break room: 'The weak crumble on the road of life'. Others laugh uncomfortably.
steps.question: This is a decisive moment. What do you do?

options.text: Contact the occupational safety representative on Eva's behalf.
Laugh along to avoid conflict.
Say out loud: 'That is not funny, it is cruel.'
Suggest a team meeting about rules without naming names.

organization_resources.title: Knowledge Base: Workplace Wellbeing
organization_resources.subtitle: Structural risks, management responsibility, and research-based knowledge for building a safe community.

ui.footer_text: "When the work community is safe, people dare to do their jobs well. When safety is missing, the consequences are seen everywhere."

content.item1:
1. Unclear roles and mandates
Creates a 'gray area' where unofficial power relations normalize.
content.item2:
2. Poor information flow
Psychological contract breaks when people feel bypassed.
content.item3:
3. Unjust management
Inner circles and favorites create susceptibility to bullying.
content.item4:
4. Illusory intervention processes
If processes are only on paper, the message is: bullying pays off.

content.summary: One prolonged bullying case can cost the organization 80,000 – 150,000 €.
content.formula: Formula: Total Cost ≈ Sick Leave + Presenteeism + Turnover + HR/Mgmt + Reputation

content.item1:
1. First Signal
Choice: Stop (react immediately) or Enable (downplay).
content.item2:
2. First Report
Choice: Stop (document) or Enable (blame sensitivity).

toxic_star.title: 1. 'Toxic Star' Dilemma
toxic_star.matrix_desc: Harvard study (Housman & Minor, 2015) shows: One "toxic star" costs the company 2x more than they produce. Assess your team members with this tool.

analysis.toxic: TOXIC STAR: Destroys team morale. Turnover costs more than their results.
analysis.star: STAR: True top performer. Hold on to them!
analysis.potential: POTENTIAL: Needs support for results, but attitude is right.
analysis.underperformer: UNDERPERFORMER: Wrong recruitment or wrong role.

toxic_star.conclusion: Conclusion: A manager has a duty to intervene even with "stars". If you let toxic behavior continue in the name of results, you drive five other experts out of the house.

legal.title: 2. Legal Backbone
legal.content_title: The Law is on Your Side

law.title: Occupational Safety Act 28 §
law.text: "The employer must, after becoming aware of harassment, take action with available means to remove the grievance."

right.title: Right to Direct
right.text: The manager has the right and duty to define what is acceptable behavior. You don't need consensus to intervene.

legal.quote: "You are not mean when you intervene – you are professional and following the law."

conflict.title: 3. Avoiding Conflict
conflict.desc: According to studies, "Laissez-faire" (let it go) leadership is most stressful for employees. Non-intervention is an active act.
conflict.exercise_title: Exposure Exercise: Say it Out Loud
conflict.exercise_desc: Read the sentences out loud. If your heart rate rises, repeat until it stabilizes.
sentences: I noticed in the meeting yesterday that you interrupted Lisa three times.
This behavior does not align with our values, and it must stop.
I want to discuss your way of giving feedback.
conflict.action: I am ready to speak directly

restorative.title: 4. Restorative Justice
restorative.intro: A bullying case doesn't end with a warning. The team is often traumatized and the position of "scapegoat" is open.

steps.title: 1. Restore Trust
steps.text: Speak to the team generally about what happened (no names), but confirm that the process has been handled and norms clarified.

steps.title: 2. Protect the Victim from Labeling
steps.text: Ensure the reporter is not left alone or treated as a "snitch". Monitor the situation actively for 3 months.
